name: Android Rust chat authentication rejection and fresh-pair recovery
summary: Maintained Rust suite passed, including 60 client integration tests and two new 401/403 rejected-chat to fresh-pair recovery cases. cargo fmt and clippy also exited 0. One opt-in live smoke was ignored. Source/test bytes were stable during execution.
scope: Host Rust client fixtures against real wiremock HTTP servers. Does not execute the server JWT verifier, Android native chat UI, hosted CI, signed candidate, physical phone, Play or public installation.
ignoredTests: live_p0_contract_smoke requires an explicitly configured live runtime and pairing inputs; it did not execute in this invocation

assertions.evidence: Both named maintained client tests reported ok; rejection emits no delta, preserves primary URL and issues exactly one request with no fallback traffic.
Each test consumes the public pair response, constructs a fresh client with its replacement token and verifies its replacement workspace in the conversation read.
Exactly four requests: rejected POST, unauthenticated pair POST, fresh-token new-message POST and fresh-token thread GET. No rejected text is replayed and no fallback request occurs.
Fresh stream emits two ordered CRLF/Unicode deltas and done, then the read returns the matching user/assistant conversation turns.
cargo test --workspace --all-targets exited 0; client suite 60 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored; existing parser/fallback/ABI guards also passed. The opt-in live test remains explicitly ignored.
cargo fmt --all -- --check and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings both exited 0 in retained execution steps.
All five retained source/test fingerprints match before and after the checks. The uncommitted test edit at execution is disclosed; no committed-source claim is inferred from headAtExecution.
